title: Third-Party Model Adapters and Runtime Contracts: Design Patterns and Integration Playbook
author: Priya Rao
body:
Summary
-------
This design spec describes a set of standardized adapter patterns and runtime contract primitives for integrating third-party (external) model endpoints into Redwood Inference. The objective is to enable safe, observable, cost-predictable, and fallback-ready use of non-Redwood models (partner-hosted or customer-hosted endpoints) while preserving platform SLOs and billing/crediting models.

Goals
-----
- Define a minimal runtime contract that every third-party model adapter must implement (capabilities, health, performance, metadata).
- Provide configuration patterns for fidelity/economics negotiation, graceful fallback, and adaptive routing.
- Specify telemetry, tracing, and billing signal requirements to maintain observability parity with native models.
- Offer a rollout and validation playbook for onboarding new adapters.

Non-Goals
---------
- This spec does not mandate how external providers internal model serving should be implemented.
- It does not replace contractual/legal terms for third-party SLAs; it defines technical primitives for runtime behavior.

Key terminology
---------------
- Adapter: Lightweight runtime component in Redwood that translates Redwood inference requests to a third-party model API and normalizes responses.
- Runtime contract: A set of API endpoints / metadata and behavioral guarantees the adapter exposes to the Redwood runtime.
- Variant: Model variant in Redwood’s catalog; an adapter-backed variant is a variant that proxies to an external model.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1) Registration: Admin registers an adapter-backed variant in the model catalog with an adapter descriptor (endpoint, auth, capacity hints, supported features).
2) Adapter runtime: The adapter runs as a sidecar or managed connector in the serving plane and exposes the standardized contract endpoints to the Redwood routing layer.
3) Request path: Routing -> Adapter contract API -> third-party model -> Adapter normalizes output -> Redwood runtime continues (KV cache, batching, post-processing).
4) Telemetry flow: Adapter MUST emit the standardized telemetry events (latency, token counts, fidelity flags) to Redwood observability ingest endpoints.

Adapter contract: required endpoints and fields
----------------------------------------------
The adapter must implement the following HTTP endpoints. Each endpoint is described in the table below. The adapter may be implemented as a container sidecar in Dedicated/Private deployments or as a hosted connector for Hosted variants.

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose | Required fields (JSON) | Response example notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| /health | GET | Liveness & readiness probe | {"uptime_s": number, "status": "ok|degraded|down", "version": string} | Used by router; TTL 5s recommended |
| /capabilities | GET | Declared features | {"max_seq": number, "supports_streaming": bool, "supported_ops": ["generate","embed","chat"]} | Used at registration and periodic refresh |
| /infer | POST | Primary request path | {"request_id": string, "input": object, "mode":"sync|stream", "budget_ms": number, "fidelity_hint": "high|medium|low"} | Adapter returns normalized out object and token counts |
| /metrics-enqueue | POST | Push telemetry events | {"request_id": string, "latency_ms": number, "tokens_in": number, "tokens_out": number, "model_variant": string} | Reduces sampling mismatch with native runtime |
| /fallback-surface | GET | Adapter-provided fallback recommendations | {"compatible_variants": [string], "confidence_score": 0.0-1.0} | Used by policy engine when errors/latency exceed thresholds |

Configuration table: adapter descriptor (catalog fields)
-----------------------------------------------------
- variant_id (string): Redwood catalog id for the adapter-backed variant.
- adapter_endpoint (url): Base URL for adapter contract endpoints.
- auth_type (enum): oauth2 | api_key | mTLS.
- capacity_hint (object serialized string): e.g., "p50_latency_ms=120;p99_latency_ms=800;throughput_rps=50".
- cost_profile (string): cost-per-token or per-call template to feed billing/crediting engine.
- fidelity_profile (string): which fidelity tier this adapter maps to for billing purposes.

Performance SLOs, thresholds, and graceful degradation
-----------------------------------------------------
- Target SLOs (adapter must support): p50 <= 150ms; p90 <= 300ms; p99 <= 1200ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens).
- If runtime sees end-to-end latency > configured budget_ms or /health reports status != ok, routing policy must mark variant as degraded and consult /fallback-surface.
- Fallback policy precedence: 1) local cached response, 2) alternative adapter-backed variant with same fidelity, 3) Redwood native lower-cost variant with fidelity negotiation, 4) synthetic short-response (graceful degradation).

Telemetry and observability requirements
--------------------------------------
- Every /infer call must enqueue a metrics event via /metrics-enqueue within 2s of completion. Telemetry fields: request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, success|error, error_class.
- Traces: adapters should propagate inbound trace headers (x-trace-id) and attach outbound traces to Redwood tracing system.
- Sampling: Default 100% token accounting for billing; sampling for detailed request traces may be configurable.

Security, data handling, and compliance constraints
--------------------------------------------------
- Customer data residency rules must be enforced: adapter deployments in Private mode MUST not route PII to external-hosted adapters without explicit contract.
- Authentication: mTLS is preferred for Dedicated/Private. OAuth2 with short-lived tokens acceptable for hosted connectors; tokens must be rotated every 24 hours in production by default.
- Audit logs: adapters must provide a pullable audit log (S3/HTTPS) or stream to Redwood audit ingest with event types: model_call, config_change, health_change.

Adapter contract extension points (optional)
-----------------------------------------
- Output post-process hooks: adapter may declare post-processing templates (JSON schema) that Redwood will apply for normalization.
- Model explainability: adapters can optionally expose a /saliency endpoint returning token-level attributions; Redwood will surface this only for customers with enabled privacy consent.

Example adapter config (catalog entry)
-------------------------------------
{ "variant_id": "ext-llm-acme-3b", "adapter_endpoint": "https://acme-adapter.example.net/v1", "auth_type": "mTLS", "capacity_hint": "p50_latency_ms=120;p99_latency_ms=900;throughput_rps=30", "cost_profile": "per_token:0.00002", "fidelity_profile": "medium" }

Onboarding and validation playbook
--------------------------------
1) Pre-onboard review: Security, Legal and Product complete checklist (data residency, liability, SLA alignment).
2) Registration: Add descriptor to model catalog in staging.
3) Smoke tests (automated): health, capabilities, infer correctness, telemetry push.
4) Performance tests: run the benchmarking suite for target token lengths (32/128/512) and record p50/p90/p99.
5) Fidelity evaluation: run representative prompt-set evals (calibration dataset) to capture quality delta vs Redwood baseline.
6) Billing test: exercise cost_profile and ensure billing engine ingests metrics events and calculates credits properly.
7) Canary rollout: route 1% traffic with automated rollback on regressions (latency or quality).
8) Full launch: move to production catalog and enable 100% routing.

Automated tests and gating
-------------------------
- Gate: no adapter variant allowed to reach >5% production traffic unless p90 latency within 2x of advertised capacity_hint p90 AND fidelity delta (measured metric) within configured tolerance.
- CI artifacts: performance CSV, fidelity evaluation report, telemetry verification JSON, security checklist signed.

Compatibility and migration considerations
----------------------------------------
- Backwards compatibility: adapters that implement /capabilities v1 must continue supporting legacy fields for 6 months with deprecation warnings in /health.
- Migration: provide a transition SDK that maps older request envelopes to new contract fields and rewrites cost_profile templates.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Product: owner of catalog and onboarding playbooks (owner_team: product).
- Runtime: eng-serving-runtime owns adapter runtime integration, routing, and policy enforcement.
- Observability: eng-platform owns telemetry ingestion, dashboarding, and alerting.
- SLAs: adapters SHOULD declare their own SLA; Redwood will surface status but will only guarantee Redwood-level SLOs for native variants unless contractual SLA exists.

Rollout roadmap and milestones (quarterly cadence)
--------------------------------------------------
- Q4 2026: spec sign-off, reference adapter SDK, telemetry contract implementation, staging onboarding of 2 partners.
- Q1 2027: integrate billing/crediting signals and end-to-end canary tooling; onboard 3 additional partners.
- Q2 2027: privacy-residency enforcement, mTLS automation, and ally program for certified adapters.

Related risks and mitigations
---------------------------
- Risk: External provider latency causes customer-visible SLO violations.
  Mitigation: aggressive degrade-and-fallback policy + preflight performance caps.
- Risk: Billing fraud / metric mismatches.
  Mitigation: cross-validate adapter telemetry with Redwood edge sampling and require signed metrics batches from adapter.

Next steps and action items
--------------------------
- Product: finalize spec and coordinate security/legal checklist by 2026-11-15.
- Eng-serving-runtime: implement adapter router stubs and /health polling by 2026-12-01.
- Eng-platform: add telemetry schema and dashboards for adapter-backed variants by 2026-12-10.

Appendix: quick-checklist for adapter readiness
----------------------------------------------
- [ ] /health implemented and returns status==ok
- [ ] /capabilities populated (max_seq, supports_streaming)
- [ ] /infer accepts budget_ms and fidelity_hint
- [ ] Telemetry events sent to /metrics-enqueue
- [ ] Auth configured and rotating per policy
- [ ] Performance reports uploaded to onboarding bucket
